ppi_focus: Recall status check by VIN at a Subaru dealer (fuel pump 21V587000, camera 18V935000).
ECU scan for tune or reflash signs and stored codes; check readiness monitors for smog.
Clutch slip and engagement height, throwout-bearing noise, synchro behaviour in 2nd/3rd.
Signs of track use: brake fluid colour, pad and rotor wear, tire shoulder wear, heat-tinted hardware, oil level and condition.
Tire DOT dates and matching brands; alignment and suspension check for lowering or replaced Sachs dampers.
Underbody and front lip/undertray scrapes; paint-meter check for unreported bodywork.
Oil leaks at the cam plates and front engine cover; any FA20 direct-injection tick vs. abnormal noise.

evidence.mission_note: A stock manual BRZ is a direct fit for the enthusiast bridge: simple, naturally aspirated, reliable, and easy to resell. The price sits above Jason's ideal band but under the ceiling, so the case rests on proving stock condition and recall and service status.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a VIN-consistent 2018 BRZ Limited with the factory Performance Package and a 6-speed manual, at 28,462 claimed miles, offered by a Southern California dealer with itemized fees. History rests on a dealer-quoted Carfax summary (one owner, no reported accident, clean title), not the report itself. Nothing is observed wrong in the captured text, but the photos and full listing were not captured. The VIN recall lookup shows the 2018 BRZ fuel-pump recall 21V587000 applies, and its completion is undocumented. Track use, tune status, tire age, clutch condition and service history are all open. The $21,895 asking price is within the fair-value range but about $2,000 above its midpoint.
